worker_notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical web text independently identifies the title Exploring the Psychological Processes That Underlie Interpersonal Forgiveness: Replication and Extension of the Model of Motivated Interpersonal Forgiveness; authors Leigh Anne N. Donovan and Joseph R. Priester; Frontiers in Psychology, 08 October 2020; DOI 10.3389/fpsyg.2020.02107. It is labelled ORIGINAL RESEARCH and contains Methods, Results, Tables 1 and 2, General Discussion, references and footnotes, supporting primary empirical report identity rather than an abstract-only excerpt. No PDF supplied; no PDF rendering possible or attempted. HTML parse has no stable page numbering; locations use headings and table/panel/path identifiers. Target ambiguity: the broad description names the complete closeness/desire/motivated-reasoning/forgiveness model but selects no path or motivated-reasoning operationalization. Table 2 has eight estimates: panel a thought negativity paths RC→thought negativity→F −0.29 (CI −0.83, 0.03); RC→CE→F 0.05 (CI −0.13, 0.23); RC→DTM→thought negativity→F 0.36 (CI 0.06, 0.88); RC→DTM→CE→F 0.01 (CI −0.07, 0.15). Panel b questionnaire-items paths RC→questionnaire items→F 0.27 (CI −0.27, 0.89); RC→CE→F 0.02 (CI −0.14, 0.18); RC→DTM→questionnaire items→F 1.35 (CI 0.68, 1.93); RC→DTM→CE→F 0.01 (CI −0.08, 0.09). These are printed Estimate entries from bootstrap OLS mediation; table does not explicitly label them unstandardized b. No candidate selected or converted. Even prioritizing the hypothesized sequential path leaves two operationalizations. Analytic N: 107 undergraduate participants is a participation count; critical Table 2 model N and missing-data handling are not explicitly reported. Positive-thought analyses removed three responses, a separate operationalization not tabulated in Table 2; do not subtract these from 107 or transfer to the tabulated models. No N derived from degrees of freedom, no mutually exclusive final-group sum. Table 2 and its accompanying mediation Results report bootstrap 95% confidence intervals and zero-inclusion decisions, without numerical p values. Independent-predictor p values in another Results section belong to different tests and were not transferred. Reported success is the authors’ overall verdict about replication of the model, not a selected Table 2 path: they explicitly state replication with the modified estimation and with thought negativity/questionnaire items; thought positivity yielded no significant mediation paths. coding_context.description: Relationship closeness leads to a desire to maintain the relationship, this desire leads to motivated reasoning, and this motivation leads to interpersonal forgiveness.
coding_context.reported_success_quote:
When motivated reasoning was measured by thought listings (in addition to the original
questionnaire items) and when the analytic estimation provided greater power, the Model
of Motivated Interpersonal Forgiveness was replicated.
